sanskrit: tad dṛṣṭvā mahad āścaryaṃ pratyakṣaṃ svargalipsayā prahṛṣṭamanasaḥ śūrāḥ kṣipraṃ jagmuḥ parasparam
english: Beholding that great marvel with their own eyes, the heroes, their hearts thrilled with longing for heaven, rushed swiftly against one another.

sanskrit: rathino rathibhiḥ sārdhaṃ citraṃ yuyudhur āhave pattayaḥ pattibhir nāgā nāgaiḥ saha hayair hayāḥ
english: Splendidly they fought in battle—chariot-warriors against chariot-warriors, foot-soldiers against foot-soldiers, elephants against elephants, and horses against horses.

sanskrit: evaṃ pravṛtte saṃgrāme gajavājijanakṣaye sainye ca rajasā vyāpte sve svāñ jaghnuḥ pare parān
english: As the battle raged thus, with its slaughter of elephants, horses, and men, and the army shrouded in dust, one's own struck down one's own, and the foe struck the foe.

sanskrit: kacākaci babhau yuddhaṃ dantādanti nakhānakhi muṣṭiyuddhaṃ niyuddhaṃ ca dehapāpmavināśanam
english: The fight blazed hair against hair, tooth against tooth, nail against nail, with fists and grappling—a struggle that destroyed both body and sin.

sanskrit: tathā vartati saṃgrāme gajavājijanakṣaye narāśvagajadehebhyaḥ prasṛtā lohitāpagā narāśvagajadehān sā vyuvāha patitān bahūn
english: As the battle ran on with its destruction of elephants, horses, and men, a river of blood streamed forth from the bodies of men, horses, and elephants, and it bore along the many fallen bodies of men, horses, and elephants.

sanskrit: narāśvagajasaṃbādhe narāśvagajasādinām lohitodā mahāghorā nadī lohitakardamā narāśvagajadehān sā vahantī bhīrubhīṣaṇī
english: In that press of men, horses, and elephants, a most terrible river whose waters were blood and whose mire was gore, fed by the slaughtered riders of men, horses, and elephants, flowed on bearing their bodies—a thing of dread to the faint-hearted.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ paramapāraṃ ca vrajanti vijayaiṣiṇaḥ gādhena ca plavantaś ca nimajjyonmajjya cāpare
english: Those who sought victory made for its farther shore, some crossing by the fords, some swimming, and yet others sinking and rising up again.

sanskrit: te tu lohitadigdhāṅgā raktavarmāyudhāmbarāḥ sasnus tasyāṃ papuś cāsṛṅ mamluś ca bharatarṣabha
english: Their limbs smeared with blood, their armor, weapons, and garments dyed red, they bathed in that river, drank of its gore, and grew faint, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: rathān aśvān narān nāgān āyudhābharaṇāni ca vasanāny atha varmāṇi hanyamānān hatān api bhūmiṃ khaṃ dyāṃ diśaś caiva prāyaḥ paśyāma lohitam
english: Chariots, horses, men, and elephants, weapons and ornaments, garments and armor, the dying and the dead, the earth, the sky, the heavens, and all the quarters—nearly everything we saw was crimson.

sanskrit: lohitasya tu gandhena sparśena ca rasena ca rūpeṇa cātiriktena śabdena ca visarpatā viṣādaḥ sumahān āsīt prāyaḥ sainyasya bhārata
english: From the smell of the blood, from its touch, its taste, its excessive sight, and the very sound of its trickling, a great despondency fell upon nearly the whole army, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tat tu viprahataṃ sainyaṃ bhīmasenamukhais tava bhūyaḥ samādravan vīrāḥ sātyakipramukhā rathāḥ
english: That sorely battered army of yours the heroes once more assailed—the chariot-warriors led by Bhīmasena and headed by Sātyaki.

sanskrit: teṣām āpatatāṃ vegam aviṣahya mahātmanām putrāṇāṃ te mahat sainyam āsīd rājan parāṅmukham
english: Unable to withstand the onset of those great-souled warriors as they charged, the mighty host of your sons turned its back in flight, O king.

sanskrit: tat prakīrṇarathāśvebhaṃ naravājisamākulam vidhvastacarmakavacaṃ praviddhāyudhakārmukam
english: That host, its chariots, horses, and elephants scattered, choked with men and steeds, its shields and armor shattered, its weapons and bows flung away—

sanskrit: vyadravat tāvakaṃ sainyaṃ loḍyamānaṃ samantataḥ siṃhārditaṃ mahāraṇye yathā gajakulaṃ tathā
english: —your army fled, churned up on every side, like a herd of elephants harried by a lion in the great forest.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tān abhidravato dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavāṃs tāvakaṃ balam krośatas tava putrasya na sma rājan nyavartata
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing the Pāṇḍavas charging upon them, your army, O king, did not turn back, though your son cried out to them.

sanskrit: tataḥ pakṣāt prapakṣāc ca prapakṣaiś cāpi dakṣiṇāt udastaśastrāḥ kuravo bhīmam abhyadravan raṇe
english: Then from the flank and from the wing, and with the wings from the right as well, the Kurus with weapons raised rushed upon Bhīma in battle.

sanskrit: karṇo 'pi dṛṣṭvā dravato dhārtarāṣṭrān parāṅmukhān haṃsavarṇān hayāgryāṃs tān praiṣīd yatra vṛkodaram
english: Karṇa too, seeing the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra fleeing with averted faces, drove his swan-white, peerless steeds to where Vṛkodara was.

sanskrit: te preṣitā mahārāja śalyenāhavaśobhinā bhīmasenarathaṃ prāpya samasajjanta vājinaḥ
english: Urged on, O great king, by Śalya who shone in battle, those horses, reaching Bhīmasena's chariot, were brought to a halt.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā karṇaṃ samāyāntaṃ bhīmaḥ krodhasamanvitaḥ matiṃ dadhre vināśāya karṇasya bharatarṣabha
english: Seeing Karṇa drawing near, Bhīma, filled with wrath, set his mind upon Karṇa's destruction, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: so 'bravīt sātyakiṃ vīraṃ dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ ca pārṣatam enaṃ rakṣata rājānaṃ dharmātmānaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram saṃśayān mahato muktaṃ kathaṃ cit prekṣato mama
english: He said to the hero Sātyaki and to Dhṛṣṭadyumna, son of Pṛṣata: 'Guard this king, the righteous-souled Yudhiṣṭhira, who, before my very eyes, has just barely escaped from a great peril.'

sanskrit: agrato me kṛto rājā chinnasarvaparicchadaḥ duryodhanasya prītyarthaṃ rādheyena durātmanā
english: 'Before me the king was stripped of all his equipage, to please Duryodhana, by the evil-souled son of Rādhā.'

sanskrit: antam adya kariṣyāmi tasya duḥkhasya pārṣata hantā vāsmi raṇe karṇaṃ sa vā māṃ nihaniṣyati saṃgrāmeṇa sughoreṇa satyam etad bravīmi vaḥ
english: 'This day, O son of Pṛṣata, I shall make an end of that sorrow. Either I shall slay Karṇa in battle, or he shall slay me in a most terrible fight—this I tell you truly.'

sanskrit: rājānam adya bhavatāṃ nyāsabhūtaṃ dadāmi vai asya saṃrakṣaṇe sarve yatadhvaṃ vigatajvarāḥ
english: 'This day I give over the king into your keeping as a sacred trust; do you all, without anxiety, strive together for his protection.'

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahābāhuḥ prāyād ādhirathiṃ prati siṃhanādena mahatā sarvāḥ saṃnādayan diśaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, the mighty-armed one advanced against the son of Adhiratha, making all the quarters resound with a great lion's roar.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tvaritam āyāntaṃ bhīmaṃ yuddhābhinandinam sūtaputram athovāca madrāṇām īśvaro vibhuḥ
english: Seeing Bhīma, who delighted in battle, swiftly approaching, the lord and sovereign of the Madras spoke thus to the son of the charioteer:

sanskrit: paśya karṇa mahābāhuṃ kruddhaṃ pāṇḍavanandanam dīrghakālārjitaṃ krodhaṃ moktukāmaṃ tvayi dhruvam
english: 'Behold, Karṇa, the mighty-armed delight of the Pāṇḍus, enraged and surely eager to pour out upon you a wrath long stored up.'

sanskrit: īdṛśaṃ nāsya rūpaṃ me dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ kadā cana abhimanyau hate karṇa rākṣase vā ghaṭotkace
english: 'Never before have I seen such a form upon him, O Karṇa—not when Abhimanyu was slain, nor when the rākṣasa Ghaṭotkaca fell.'

sanskrit: trailokyasya samastasya śaktaḥ kruddho nivāraṇe bibharti yādṛśaṃ rūpaṃ kālāgnisadṛśaṃ śubham
english: 'In his wrath, fit to hold back the whole of the three worlds, he wears a form fair yet terrible, like the fire of the world's end.'

sanskrit: iti bruvati rādheyaṃ madrāṇām īśvare nṛpa abhyavartata vai karṇaṃ krodhadīpto vṛkodaraḥ
english: As the lord of the Madras spoke thus to the son of Rādhā, O king, Vṛkodara, ablaze with anger, bore down upon Karṇa.

sanskrit: tathāgataṃ tu saṃprekṣya bhīmaṃ yuddhābhinandinam abravīd vacanaṃ śalyaṃ rādheyaḥ prahasann iva
english: Beholding Bhīma, who rejoiced in battle, come on in that fashion, the son of Rādhā, smiling as it were, spoke these words to Śalya:

sanskrit: yad uktaṃ vacanaṃ me 'dya tvayā madrajaneśvara bhīmasenaṃ prati vibho tat satyaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: 'The words you have spoken to me this day concerning Bhīmasena, O lord of the Madra people, O mighty one, are true—of this there is no doubt.'

sanskrit: eṣa śūraś ca vīraś ca krodhanaś ca vṛkodaraḥ nirapekṣaḥ śarīre ca prāṇataś ca balādhikaḥ
english: 'This Vṛkodara is brave and heroic and wrathful, heedless of his own body and of his very life, and surpassing in strength.'

sanskrit: ajñātavāsaṃ vasatā virāṭanagare tadā draupadyāḥ priyakāmena kevalaṃ bāhusaṃśrayāt gūḍhabhāvaṃ samāśritya kīcakaḥ sagaṇo hataḥ
english: 'When he dwelt in concealment in the city of Virāṭa, to do a kindness to Draupadī, relying on the strength of his arms alone, keeping his identity hidden, he slew Kīcaka together with his kinsmen.'

sanskrit: so 'dya saṃgrāmaśirasi saṃnaddhaḥ krodhamūrcchitaḥ kiṃkarodyatadaṇḍena mṛtyunāpi vrajed raṇam
english: 'This day, at the head of the battle, armed and frenzied with rage, he would march into the fray even against Death himself with uplifted, ready rod, the servant of Yama.'

sanskrit: cirakālābhilaṣito mamāyaṃ tu manorathaḥ arjunaṃ samare hanyāṃ māṃ vā hanyād dhanaṃjayaḥ sa me kadā cid adyaiva bhaved bhīmasamāgamāt
english: 'But this is my heart's desire, long cherished: that I should slay Arjuna in battle, or that Dhanaṃjaya should slay me. Through this meeting with Bhīma, that wish of mine may perhaps be fulfilled this very day.'

sanskrit: nihate bhīmasene tu yadi vā virathīkṛte abhiyāsyati māṃ pārthas tan me sādhu bhaviṣyati atra yan manyase prāptaṃ tac chīghraṃ saṃpradhāraya
english: 'For if Bhīmasena be slain, or be deprived of his chariot, then Pārtha will come against me—and that will be well for me. Resolve quickly upon what you deem fit here.'

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tu vacanaṃ rādheyasya mahātmanaḥ uvāca vacanaṃ śalyaḥ sūtaputraṃ tathāgatam
english: Hearing these words of the great-souled son of Rādhā, Śalya spoke thus to the son of the charioteer as he came on:

sanskrit: abhiyāsi mahābāho bhīmasenaṃ mahābalam nirasya bhīmasenaṃ tu tataḥ prāpsyasi phalgunam
english: 'Advance, O mighty-armed one, against the mighty Bhīmasena; and when you have driven Bhīmasena off, then you shall meet Phalguna.'

sanskrit: yas te kāmo 'bhilaṣitaś cirāt prabhṛti hṛdgataḥ sa vai saṃpatsyate karṇa satyam etad bravīmi te
english: 'That desire which you have cherished in your heart since long ago shall surely be fulfilled, O Karṇa—this I tell you truly.'

sanskrit: evam ukte tataḥ karṇaḥ śalyaṃ punar abhāṣata hantāham arjunaṃ saṃkhye māṃ vā hantā dhanaṃjayaḥ yuddhe manaḥ samādhāya yāhi yāhīty acodayat
english: Thus addressed, Karṇa spoke again to Śalya: 'I shall slay Arjuna in the encounter, or Dhanaṃjaya shall slay me. Fix your mind upon the battle—drive on, drive on!' he urged.

sanskrit: tataḥ prāyād rathenāśu śalyas tatra viśāṃ pate yatra bhīmo maheṣvāso vyadrāvayata vāhinīm
english: Then Śalya swiftly drove the chariot, O lord of the people, to where Bhīma, the great archer, was putting the host to rout.

sanskrit: tatas tūryaninādaś ca bherīṇāṃ ca mahāsvanaḥ udatiṣṭhata rājendra karṇabhīmasamāgame
english: Then the blare of trumpets and the great clamor of kettledrums arose, O lord of kings, at the meeting of Karṇa and Bhīma.

sanskrit: bhīmaseno 'tha saṃkruddhas tava sainyaṃ durāsadam nārācair vimalais tīkṣṇair diśaḥ prādrāvayad balī
english: Then the mighty Bhīmasena, filled with wrath, with bright sharp iron shafts drove your hard-to-assail army fleeing in all directions.

sanskrit: sa saṃnipātas tumulo bhīmarūpo viśāṃ pate āsīd raudro mahārāja karṇapāṇḍavayor mṛdhe tato muhūrtād rājendra pāṇḍavaḥ karṇam ādravat
english: That clash was tumultuous and terrible in aspect, O lord of the people, fierce indeed, in the battle between Karṇa and the Pāṇḍava; and after a moment, O lord of kings, the Pāṇḍava charged upon Karṇa.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya karṇo vaikartano vṛṣaḥ ājaghānorasi kruddho nārācena stanāntare punaś cainam ameyātmā śaravarṣair avākirat
english: Seeing him charge on, Karṇa Vaikartana, the bull among men, struck him in wrath upon the chest, between the breasts, with an iron shaft; then that one of measureless soul overwhelmed him with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: sa viddhaḥ sūtaputreṇa chādayām āsa patribhiḥ vivyādha niśitaiḥ karṇa navabhir nataparvabhiḥ
english: Pierced by the son of the charioteer, he covered Karṇa over with feathered shafts and struck him with nine sharp, smooth-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: tasya karṇo dhanurmadhye dvidhā ciccheda patriṇā atha taṃ chinnadhanvānam abhyavidhyat stanāntare nārācena sutīkṣṇena sarvāvaraṇabhedinā
english: Karṇa cut his bow in two at the middle with a feathered shaft; then, when his bow was severed, he struck him between the breasts with a most sharp iron shaft that pierced through all armor.

sanskrit: so 'nyat kārmukam ādāya sūtaputraṃ vṛkodaraḥ rājan marmasu marmajño viddhvā suniśitaiḥ śaraiḥ nanāda balavan nādaṃ kampayann iva rodasī
english: Taking up another bow, Vṛkodara, O king, who knew the vital points, pierced the son of the charioteer in his vitals with keenly whetted shafts and roared a mighty roar, as if to shake heaven and earth.

sanskrit: taṃ karṇaḥ pañcaviṃśatyā nārācānāṃ samārdayat madotkaṭaṃ vane dṛptam ulkābhir iva kuñjaram
english: Karṇa tormented him with five-and-twenty iron shafts, as one might torment with firebrands a rut-maddened, haughty elephant in the forest.

sanskrit: tataḥ sāyakabhinnāṅgaḥ pāṇḍavaḥ krodhamūrcchitaḥ saṃrambhāmarṣatāmrākṣaḥ sūtaputravadhecchayā
english: Then the Pāṇḍava, his limbs torn by the arrows, frenzied with rage, his eyes coppery with fury and indignation, in his desire to slay the son of the charioteer—

sanskrit: sa kārmuke mahāvegaṃ bhārasādhanam uttamam girīṇām api bhettāraṃ sāyakaṃ samayojayat
english: —fitted to his bow an arrow of great speed, of supreme striking power, a shaft that could cleave even mountains.

sanskrit: vikṛṣya balavac cāpam ā karṇād atimārutiḥ taṃ mumoca maheṣvāsaḥ kruddhaḥ karṇajighāṃsayā
english: Drawing the bow with might back to his ear, that surpassing son of the Wind-god, the great archer, in his wrath let the shaft fly, eager to slay Karṇa.

sanskrit: sa visṛṣṭo balavatā bāṇo vajrāśanisvanaḥ adārayad raṇe karṇaṃ vajravega ivācalam
english: Loosed by the mighty one, that arrow, with the sound of thunderbolt and lightning, rent Karṇa in the battle as a thunderbolt's force cleaves a mountain.

sanskrit: sa bhīmasenābhihato sūtaputraḥ kurūdvaha niṣasāda rathopasthe visaṃjñaḥ pṛtanāpatiḥ
english: Struck by Bhīmasena, the son of the charioteer, O perpetuator of the Kurus, that commander of armies sank down senseless upon the floor of his chariot.

sanskrit: tato madrādhipo dṛṣṭvā visaṃjñaṃ sūtanandanam apovāha rathenājau karṇam āhavaśobhinam
english: Then the lord of the Madras, seeing the son of the charioteer fallen senseless, bore Karṇa, who shone in battle, away from the field upon his chariot.

sanskrit: tataḥ parājite karṇe dhārtarāṣṭrīṃ mahācamūm vyadrāvayad bhīmaseno yathendro dānavīṃ camūm
english: Then, Karṇa being vanquished, Bhīmasena routed the great host of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, as Indra routed the host of the Dānavas.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca suduṣkaram idaṃ karma kṛtaṃ bhīmena saṃjaya yena karṇo mahābāhū rathopasthe nipātitaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: A most difficult deed has been done by Bhīma, O Saṃjaya, in that the mighty-armed Karṇa was struck down upon the floor of his chariot.

sanskrit: karṇo hy eko raṇe hantā sṛñjayān pāṇḍavaiḥ saha iti duryodhanaḥ sūta prābravīn māṃ muhur muhuḥ
english: 'Karṇa alone in battle will slay the Sṛñjayas together with the Pāṇḍavas'—so, O charioteer, did Duryodhana tell me again and again.

sanskrit: parājitaṃ tu rādheyaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmena saṃyuge tataḥ paraṃ kim akarot putro duryodhano mama
english: Seeing the son of Rādhā vanquished by Bhīma in the encounter, what then did my son Duryodhana do thereafter?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca vibhrāntaṃ prekṣya rādheyaṃ sūtaputraṃ mahāhave mahatyā senayā rājan sodaryān samabhāṣata
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing the son of Rādhā, the son of the charioteer, reeling in that great battle, the king with his vast army spoke to his own brothers:

sanskrit: śīghraṃ gacchata bhadraṃ vo rādheyaṃ parirakṣata bhīmasenabhayāgādhe majjantaṃ vyasanārṇave
english: 'Go quickly—good fortune to you—and protect the son of Rādhā, who is sinking in the fathomless ocean of calamity that is the terror of Bhīmasena.'

sanskrit: te tu rājñā samādiṣṭā bhīmasenajighāṃsavaḥ abhyavartanta saṃkruddhāḥ pataṃgā iva pāvakam
english: Commanded thus by the king, eager to slay Bhīmasena, they advanced in fury like moths upon a flame.

sanskrit: śrutāyur durdharaḥ krātho vivitsur vikaṭaḥ samaḥ niṣaṅgī kavacī pāśī tathā nandopanandakau
english: Śrutāyus, Durdhara, Krātha, Vivitsu, Vikaṭa, Sama, Niṣaṅgin, Kavacin, Pāśin, and Nanda and Upananda—

sanskrit: duṣpradharṣaḥ subāhuś ca vātavegasuvarcasau dhanurgrāho durmadaś ca tathā sattvasamaḥ sahaḥ
english: —Duṣpradharṣa and Subāhu, Vātavega and Suvarcas, Dhanurgrāha and Durmada, and likewise Sattvasama and Saha—

sanskrit: ete rathaiḥ parivṛtā vīryavanto mahābalāḥ bhīmasenaṃ samāsādya samantāt paryavārayan te vyamuñcañ śaravrātān nānāliṅgān samantataḥ
english: —these valiant and mighty ones, surrounded by their chariots, having reached Bhīmasena, beset him on every side and loosed upon him from all directions volleys of arrows of many marks.

sanskrit: sa tair abhyardyamānas tu bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ teṣām āpatatāṃ kṣipraṃ sutānāṃ te narādhipa rathaiḥ pañcāśatā sārdhaṃ pañcāśan nyahanad rathān
english: Sorely pressed by them, the mighty Bhīmasena swiftly slew, of those sons of yours rushing upon him, O lord of men, fifty chariot-warriors along with their fifty chariots.

sanskrit: vivitsos tu tataḥ kruddho bhallenāpāharac chiraḥ sakuṇḍalaśirastrāṇaṃ pūrṇacandropamaṃ tadā bhīmena ca mahārāja sa papāta hato bhuvi
english: Then, in his wrath, with a broad-headed shaft Bhīma struck off Vivitsu's head, decked with earrings and helmet and like the full moon; and so, O great king, slain by Bhīma, he fell to the earth.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā nihataṃ śūraṃ bhrātaraḥ sarvataḥ prabho abhyadravanta samare bhīmaṃ bhīmaparākramam
english: Seeing that hero slain, his brothers from every side, O lord, charged in battle upon Bhīma of dreadful prowess.

sanskrit: tato 'parābhyāṃ bhallābhyāṃ putrayos te mahāhave jahāra samare prāṇān bhīmo bhīmaparākramaḥ
english: Then with two other broad-headed shafts, Bhīma of dreadful prowess took the lives of two of your sons in that great battle.

sanskrit: tau dharām anvapadyetāṃ vātarugṇāv iva drumau vikaṭaś ca samaś cobhau devagarbhasamau nṛpa
english: Both fell to the earth like trees broken by the wind—Vikaṭa and Sama, the two of them, fair as the sons of gods, O king.

sanskrit: tatas tu tvarito bhīmaḥ krāthaṃ ninye yamakṣayam nārācena sutīkṣṇena sa hato nyapatad bhuvi
english: Then Bhīma in haste sent Krātha to the abode of Yama; struck by a most sharp iron shaft, he fell slain to the earth.

sanskrit: hāhākāras tatas tīvraḥ saṃbabhūva janeśvara vadhyamāneṣu te rājaṃs tadā putreṣu dhanviṣu
english: Then a piercing cry of woe arose, O lord of men, as your bow-bearing sons were slain, O king.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ saṃlulite sainye bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ nandopanandau samare prāpayad yamasādanam
english: When their host was thrown into disorder, the mighty Bhīmasena dispatched Nanda and Upananda in battle to the dwelling of Yama.

sanskrit: tatas te prādravan bhītāḥ putrās te vihvalīkṛtāḥ bhīmasenaṃ raṇe dṛṣṭvā kālāntakayamopamam
english: Then your sons, stricken and dismayed, fled in terror, beholding Bhīmasena in the battle like Yama the all-ending destroyer at the world's close.

sanskrit: putrāṃs te nihatān dṛṣṭvā sūtaputro mahāmanāḥ haṃsavarṇān hayān bhūyaḥ prāhiṇod yatra pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Seeing your sons slain, the high-minded son of the charioteer again drove his swan-white steeds to where the Pāṇḍava was.

sanskrit: te preṣitā mahārāja madrarājena vājinaḥ bhīmasenarathaṃ prāpya samasajjanta vegitāḥ
english: Urged on by the king of the Madras, O great king, those horses, reaching Bhīmasena's chariot at speed, were brought to a stand.

sanskrit: sa saṃnipātas tumulo ghorarūpo viśāṃ pate āsīd raudro mahārāja karṇapāṇḍavayor mṛdhe
english: That clash was tumultuous and terrible of aspect, O lord of the people, fierce indeed, O great king, in the battle between Karṇa and the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā mama mahārāja tau sametau mahārathau āsīd buddhiḥ kathaṃ nūnam etad adya bhaviṣyati
english: Seeing those two great chariot-warriors joined in combat, O great king, the thought arose in me: how, indeed, will this turn out this day?

sanskrit: tato muhūrtād rājendra nātikṛcchrād dhasann iva virathaṃ bhīmakarmāṇaṃ bhīmaṃ karṇaś cakāra ha
english: Then in a moment, O lord of kings, without much effort, smiling as it were, Karṇa made Bhīma of terrible deeds bereft of his chariot.

sanskrit: viratho bharataśreṣṭhaḥ prahasann anilopamaḥ gadāhasto mahābāhur apatat syandanottamāt
english: Bereft of his chariot, that best of the Bhāratas, laughing aloud, the mighty-armed one, peer of the wind, mace in hand, leapt down from his excellent car.
